title: Does it matter how far back a fading ally looks: the last partner or the whole memory?
lede: allies who fade by the share of R among only their last k partners (k = 1, 3, 5, 9) tip about as many crowds as the whole-memory rule: at c = 0.01 and robots 0.10, 11 to 12 of 12 against 10 for constant fading; at c = 0.03, robots 0.15, 12 of 12 against 10. Differences between k are one crowd of 12. Stylised
summary: The society-allywatch crowd (200 people, memory 9, error 0.02, 20% allies, 12 seeds, 1500 rounds) with allies who convert at rate c×f, f the share of their last k partners who walked the other way, for k = 1, 3, 5 and 9 (9 reproduces society-allywatch exactly). At c = 0.01 and robot share 0.10 all look-backs tip 11–12 of 12 crowds against 10 for constant fading; at c = 0.03 and 0.15 robots all tip 12 of 12 against 10. In the marginal cell (c = 0.03, robots 0.10) it is 2, 3, 3, 4 of 12 against 0, a monotone but one-crowd-per-step trend that 12 seeds cannot separate. Stylised: the rule and c are assumed, not measured; simulated walkers only.
